---
title: "Scope Model Reference"
description: "Project, Environment, and Collection -- complete reference"
---

## Overview

Appbay has three organizational concepts. Each controls a different aspect of how apps are grouped, configured, and deployed.

| Concept | Controls | Compose mapping | Cardinality |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Project** | Variable namespace | Which `project.yaml` vars are loaded | Single per app |
| **Environment** | Variable values | Which `.env` gets rendered | Single per deploy |
| **Collection** | App selection | Which `docker compose up` calls are made | Multi per app |

Collection is NOT part of variable resolution — it is a selector only. Variable resolution is prefix-based: `${{project.KEY}}` reads from `project.yaml`, `${{environment.KEY}}` reads from `environment.yaml`, and `${{service.KEY}}` reads from service vars. Each prefix targets exactly one store; there is no cascading fallthrough.

## Project

A project is a variable scope namespace. It controls which `projects/<project>/project.yaml` vars are loaded for `${{project.KEY}}` resolution. Container naming, volume naming, and network naming are all derived from the **app name**, not the project field.

```yaml
# appbay.yaml
project: homelab
```

### What it controls at Compose runtime

- Container names: `appbay.ollama.web` (pattern: `appbay.<app>.<service>` — project is NOT part of the container name)
- Volume prefixes: `ollama_data` (pattern: `<app>_<volume>`)
- Compose project name: determined by Docker Compose from the render directory name (e.g., `ollama` from `renders/ollama/`) — no `-p` flag is passed by Appbay
- Shared network: `appbay_shared` (the default; configurable via `shared_network:` in `appbay.yaml`)
- Variable namespace: `${{project.DOMAIN}}` resolves from `projects/homelab/project.yaml`

### When to use multiple projects

- Separate variable namespaces on the same host (e.g., `homelab` vs `work-lab` with different domains and TZ)
- Apps that need different project-level variable values to share the same config keys

**Default:** If `project` is omitted from `appbay.yaml`, it defaults to `"default"`.

## Environment

An environment is a deployment variant. It determines which variable values are used -- different domains, secrets, ports, or feature flags for the same apps.

```yaml
# appbay.yaml
environment: prod
```

### What it controls at Compose runtime

- Which variables are rendered into `.env` files
- Which secret URIs are resolved (prod secrets vs dev secrets)
- Which cert resolver is used (staging vs production Let's Encrypt)
- Variable namespace: `${{environment.DB_HOST}}` resolves from `environments/prod/environment.yaml`

### Typical environments

| Name | Domain | Certs | Secrets |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prod` | `homelab.example.com` | Production Let's Encrypt | Real secrets |
| `dev` | `localhost` | Staging certs | Dev secrets |
| `staging` | `staging.example.com` | Production-like | Separate data |

**Default:** If `environment` is omitted, defaults to `"default"`.

The environment for an app is set in `appbay.yaml`. To deploy with a different environment, set `environment:` in `appbay.yaml` or maintain separate app directories per environment.

## Collection

A collection is an operational grouping -- a named set of apps that are deployed, restarted, or stopped together. Collections are purely a selection mechanism.

```yaml
# appbay.yaml
collection: [ai-stack, gpu-apps]
```

### What it controls

Which apps are included in a batch operation. Nothing else.

### What it does NOT control

- Variable values (use environment for that)
- Naming prefixes (use project for that)
- Network isolation (use project for that)

### Multi-valued

An app can belong to multiple collections:

```yaml
# ollama
collection: [ai-stack, gpu-apps]

# jellyfin
collection: [media, gpu-apps]
```

### CLI usage

```bash
appbay up --collection ai-stack          # Deploy all ai-stack apps
appbay up ollama webui                   # Deploy specific apps (no collection needed)
appbay down ollama webui tts             # Stop apps by name
appbay restart ollama jellyfin           # Restart apps by name
```

## Variable resolution

Variables are resolved by scope prefix — each `${{scope.KEY}}` reference targets exactly one variable store. There is no cascading fallthrough.

Collection is NOT part of variable resolution. It is a selector, not a scope level.

### Variable reference syntax

| Syntax | Resolves from | Only from |
|---|---|---|
| `${{project.KEY}}` | `etc/projects/<name>/project.yaml` | project store only |
| `${{environment.KEY}}` | `etc/projects/<name>/environments/<env>.yaml` | environment store only |
| `${{service.KEY}}` | Service-level vars in `appbay.yaml` or `.env` | service store only |

Undefined variable references produce explicit errors with the scope and key name. Appbay never silently substitutes empty strings.

### Resolution example

```yaml
# projects/homelab/project.yaml
vars:
  DOMAIN: home.lan
  TZ: UTC

# projects/homelab/environments/prod.yaml
vars:
  DOMAIN: homelab.example.com    # separate environment-scope value, does NOT override project-scope
  TZ: America/New_York
```

Resolution of `${{project.DOMAIN}}` in any environment:
- Returns `home.lan` — resolved from `project.yaml` only

Resolution of `${{environment.DOMAIN}}`:
- In `prod`: returns `homelab.example.com` — resolved from `prod.yaml`
- In `dev` (if `dev.yaml` has no `DOMAIN`): compile error — undefined variable

### Magic generators

| Generator | Output | Persisted? |
|---|---|---|
| `${password:N}` | Random N-character password | Yes -- stored in `generated-values.yaml` |
| `${uuid}` | Random UUID v4 | Yes |
| `${base64:N}` | Random N-byte base64 string | Yes |
| `${hash}` | Deterministic hash of (project + env + service + key) | No -- always reproducible |
| `${timestamp}` | Current ISO timestamp | No -- evaluated at render time |

Generated values are keyed by `(project, environment, service, var_name)`. Once generated, they are reused on subsequent compiles to ensure deterministic output.

## Compose runtime mapping

When you run `appbay up --collection ai-stack`:

```
1. Select apps tagged with collection: ai-stack
   -> [ollama, webui, tts]

2. For each app, resolve variables:
   ${{project.KEY}} from project.yaml (homelab), ${{environment.KEY}} from environment.yaml (prod), ${{service.KEY}} from app .env

3. Compile each app:
   upstream transform -> overlays -> traits -> render

4. Execute each app as a separate Compose project:
   docker compose -f renders/ollama/docker-compose.rendered.yml up -d
   docker compose -f renders/webui/docker-compose.rendered.yml up -d
   docker compose -f renders/tts/docker-compose.rendered.yml up -d
```

Each app is an independent Compose project. They communicate via shared networks (e.g., `appbay_shared`), not via Compose's internal service discovery.

## Filesystem layout

```
$APPBAY_HOME/
  etc/
    projects/
      homelab/                          # Project boundary
        project.yaml                    # Project-level vars
        environments/
          prod.yaml                     # Prod variable values
          dev.yaml                      # Dev variable values
    apps/
      ollama/                           # App definition
        appbay.yaml                     # project: homelab, collection: [ai-stack]
        docker-compose.yml
      jellyfin/
        appbay.yaml                     # project: homelab, collection: [media]
        docker-compose.yml
```

## Reserved keys vs tags

| Type | Keys | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| **Reserved** | `project`, `environment`, `collection`, `operator`, `service` | Fixed meaning -- drives Appbay behavior |
| **Tags** | Anything via `tags:` | No fixed meaning -- UI filtering and bulk ops only |

## Anti-patterns

### Do not use collections for variable scoping

```yaml
# WRONG: no collection-level variable resolution exists
# RIGHT: use environment or app-level overrides
environment: prod
```

### Do not use projects for operational grouping

```yaml
# WRONG
project: ai-apps     # Just for grouping
project: media-apps

# RIGHT
project: homelab
collection: [ai-stack]    # ollama
collection: [media]       # jellyfin
```

### Do not use environments for selecting different app sets

```yaml
# WRONG
environment: ai-mode
environment: media-mode

# RIGHT
environment: prod
collection: [ai-stack]    # appbay up --collection ai-stack
collection: [media]       # appbay up --collection media
```
